tests: the shared register refuses a second environment with one line naming the holder and leaves the register sha unchanged

consumesExternalOutput.program: git ls-remote / git commit-tree / git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: src/exclusion.ts and src/commands/init.ts both spawn git and read its verdicts, so SPAWN_GREP matches them and red-witness rule (f) binds every witness whose members touch them. The cited capture is a REAL forced contention on a bare repository, captured 2026-09-17 with git 2.43.0 and node v26.6.0: it records that git commit-tree exits 128 with `fatal: empty ident name` when no identity is in scope, that the exact-sha --force-with-lease form is ACCEPTED against the value the register holds and REFUSED with `! [rejected] ... (stale info)` against any other, that ls-remote against a path that is not a repository exits 128 while ls-remote for an absent ref exits 0 with empty output, and that the FIRST stderr line of every push here is a push negotiation warning that is byte-identical on the accepted and the refused arms. That last fact is why src/exclusion.ts selects git's own `! [rejected]` marker instead of the first line, and it is the reason a hand-written expectation would have been indistinguishable from a fabricated one (T-003). The named test reads the capture and then reproduces the accept and refuse arms against a live scratch repository. The two members are structurally different halves of the same class: member 0 keeps the layer running and makes the register's HELD state read as free, and member 1 disables the layer for every fleet by pointing the declaration read at a path no fleet home occupies. Both put the second environment back in the dangerous state M4-P20 measured, where two clones of one fleet hold live leases at once.
